method: 15 grades sampled across all 6 searches (11 local, 4 online). Every grade whose verdict occurs fewer than 8 times was included (local_exists 'no', page_access 'error' and 'blocked', sells_product 'equivalent'), which filled 9 slots and skewed the sample toward local results; the other 6 were drawn by sells_product and section. Because the sampling script listed those 9 in verdict order, the auditor knew one original field for each of them before grading: local_exists for local:loc47NNJOGVBFVCUA3RSVIGOHSCRYCN6S4QYAAAAAAA=:6, local:loc4PVLJSKNNBZCEBJH6PKCQLUSSYAQCDYCOAAAAAAA=:5, local:loc4QKYK4ZMNBVCEAYAHFHJ4HUSSYBSGY4VNAAAAAAA=:4; page_access for local:loc4DZC6ORVCG5CUA3MRB7KW7RSRYDM7FZO6AAAAAAA=:8, local:loc4MW36AVUL7FBUBGEC3IKLJSSSYDIBTGM6AAAAAAA=:12, local:loc4M6CBFQMTBFCEB7XRXFXKLT2SYDXINXMTAAAAAAA=:10, local:loc425WVB65NBVCEATM7DVYF3VSSYDVMT3GZAAAAAAA=:12, local:loc4RK6WD3GOF5CUBKAVJM3MGICSYBL3ZDHJAAAAAAA=:4; sells_product for local:loc4FNQKP7L3EZCUB5PL6O6SXWKRYC7STEYFAAAAAAA=:13. All other fields were graded blind, then compared. Graded per eval/README.md; local_exists 'no' where the shop's own site could not be reached is marked 'weak no' in the reason, since the schema has no 'unknown' for that field.

findings: sells_product: full agreement (15/15), including the 7 'unknown' grades, all of which were unreachable or catalog-less pages.

local_exists: 5 of 6 disagreements are one rubric gap, not a factual dispute. When a local shop's own site is unreachable, the original grader used 'n/a' and the audit used 'no'. The schema reserves 'n/a' for online results and has no 'unknown', so neither is clearly right; precision treats both the same (only 'yes' counts), so the gap does not move the headline number. Adding 'unknown' to local_exists would remove it.

local_exists and page_access on acehardware.com/store-details/17984: the original grader got a Cloudflare block page twice; the audit got the store page normally and could confirm the address. Likely transient or session-dependent bot blocking rather than a grading error, but it means one 'blocked' in the bot-blocked rate may not reproduce.

page_access 'ok' vs 'error' on dead pages is inconsistent in the original grades: a host placeholder ('temporarily unavailable', cmcstaff.com) was graded 'error', while a Shopify 'Store unavailable' placeholder and an Orvis 404 were graded 'ok'. The audit graded all three 'error'. The rubric should say whether a page that loads but shows a 404 or deactivated-store notice is 'ok' or 'error'.

Both graders scored sells_product for local chain stores (DICK'S, Cabela's) from the chain's online catalog, because the linked page is a store-locator page that offers nothing. The rubric says 'the page offers the product', so the 15/15 sells_product agreement partly reflects a shared, unwritten reading of the rubric for local results.
